feat(facts): record a session out of the daemon, replay it in the demo, refuse another facts version (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.qg5) (#629)

* feat(facts): record writes a session's stream out of the daemon, the demo replays the file frame by frame, and another facts version is refused (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.qg5)

A recording is a header, then documents and requests with their instants.
The session recorder follows the render cache's current view (one writer of
the cache's view map fires the observer), request lines are noted where the
request path settles a view, and the file is created new and closed after
N seconds or at daemon close. The wire verb is a held request the connection
starts only while its client waits. The demo splits into load and play, one
view-and-print path, with --recording choosing the recording arm on a held
clock (moved to src/). cc-candybar record exits 1 when no request arrived.

Tests run on the render-cache rig rather than an in-worker daemon, because
the boot ratchet only falls.

* fix(facts): a recording lets go of its view when a write ends it, stops when its client leaves, writes whole lines, and refuses a span no timer holds (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.qg5)

A failed first write ended the recording before its reaction's disposer
was the recording's, so the reaction outlived it. The client's hang-up now
aborts the held work; a close's error is the recording's; appendFileSync
writes the whole line; one parse of a recording's span serves CLI and
daemon and caps it at what setTimeout holds; a request line of another
session is refused; the README says the config's own sources still run.

* fix(facts): a replay's clock starts at its first request, a recording no request arrived in leaves no file, a write-ended recording is the daemon's failure, and a recording follows a view entered inside a batch (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.qg5)

The recorder's reaction fires immediately again and owns its disposer
through the effect's own handle, so neither a failed first write nor a
batch loses a document. The README and help name the config a replay
needs, and say a config's own shell and file sources are not in a
recording (the cure is candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.d8n).

* fix(facts): a recording the daemon's close cut short says so, a record request after the close is refused for it, the file is owner-only, and a held connection reads nothing more (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.qg5)

* fix(facts): a recording with no request leaves no file however it ended (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.qg5)

chore(release): set `package.json` to 1.198.1 [skip ci]

## [1.198.1](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/compare/v1.198.0...v1.198.1) (2026-11-06)

### Bug Fixes

* **ci:** a failed early step shows its own red step, not the three that restate it (candybar-testing-0x6u.dsu) ([#630](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/issues/630)) ([6933237](https://github.com/promptctl/cc-candybar/commit/6933237709e563a9f5c545898d2df59c76238cd3))
fix(test): the close case proves the daemon's own work reached the leak record, and every close failure is reported (candybar-testing-0x6u.6f3)
fix(test): review of the leak fix — the dead baseline goes, a failed close no longer strands the rest, the close-all case closes in finally (candybar-testing-0x6u.6f3)

fix(test): the daemon close case counts only its own timers, and no file leaves a git provider open (candybar-testing-0x6u.6f3)

The close case read every timer the jest worker armed. A git provider an
earlier file never closed keeps passing on its period, so its timers landed in
whichever file ran next and the case failed on CI order, not on the daemon:
the daemon builds no git state in this case, and a probe that leaks one
provider before it reproduces the CI stacks.

The case now counts resources made inside its own async work. The git-cache
file closes every provider it builds after each case (75 built, 33 closed by
hand), and two watcher cases close in a finally.

fix(pricing): the shared load keeps a throw as the bundled rates, said once; comments state what the one git option set reads and where a read's throw is logged (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.xb3)
test(facts): the seam's providers price by the bundled rates (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.xb3)

fix(pricing): the load ends with the daemon's closing signal and never rejects; the day's copy is one atomic file with no lock, and a table missing a rate the cost reads is refused (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.xb3)
fix(pricing): a daemon prices by an adapter it closes: one table loaded once, no pooled socket, and the bundled rates under test (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.xb3)
test(facts): name the doctor's closure tests for what they protect (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.xb3)
fix(facts): the wait's comment names every session; the doctor's namespace-read test returns (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.xb3)

chore(facts): delete the wants closure (candybar-gather-renderer-76bb.6pj.xb3)

The facts document is total, so the question "which fields does this config
read" has no caller with a reason. Every session now gathers every built-in:
git runs one constant option set (forge lookup included), every declared
plugin source is held, and burn, block and autocompact's context cap are always
composed. A view's declaration depends on the request alone, so a preset pick
moves no hold.

Deleted: the wants function, the needed-prefix builders, the sources-read walk,
the closure parameter through declare/refresh/read/project, the PR reads gate,
the git options derived from the closure, `Gathered`, `declaredSources`, and the
view's preset reaction. The doctor's data-needs walk stays and now owns its own
per-segment path closure, since it answers what a config would read.

The bar is byte-identical; the payload golden gains the keys that were gated
(block, burn, metrics, activity, tmux and the like on presets that did not read
them). Tests that asserted gating are deleted; the fold-edge cases they covered
(partials, helpers handed a dict) move to the doctor's path closure.
